title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a roadmap, drawn as a diagram, for the axiomatic part of Grothendieck's fourth draft of 'Analysis situs' (Chapter VIII, June–July 1986). It belongs to the programme of 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) announced in Esquisse d'un programme. The basic object is a 'magasin' (store or warehouse). A magasin is a set M of 'figures', taken as primitives and not necessarily as sets of points. It carries some of the following relations:
- ≤, read as incidence/inclusion of figures;
- ≪ or ≪̊, a 'lies in the interior of' or 'well-inside' relation;
- |∘|, apartness or disjointness;
- a family Σ_M of 'ombres' (shadows, i.e. supports), which are subsets of M or of a set L of 'lieux' (places).

The diagram orders these structures from most general to most special, with page references to the axioms:

1. Magasins généraux: (M, ≤, ≪, |∘|), axioms Mag 1–4 (p.22), with Σ_M ⊂ P(M).

2. Magasins locaux: (M, ≤, ≪̊, |∘|_L), axioms Magloc 1–3 (p.23).
   - Supports now lie in the lieux: Σ_M ⊂ P(L).
   - He warns that the inclusions do not necessarily commute with A∩B (or with arbitrary ⋂), and that Sup(A,B) need not exist.
   - Key compatibility: for A, B ∈ Σ_M, A∩B = ∅ ⇔ A|∘|B. Disjoint supports means the figures are apart.

3. Magasins à ombres fidèles: (M, ≤, ≪̊), axioms Magfid 1–2 (p.31).
   - The map X ↦ Omb°(X) (open shadow) is a faithful support function.
   - The same rule, disjoint shadows ⇔ apartness, holds.

4. Magasins ponctuaires, both local and faithful: (M, ≤, ≪), axioms Magponc 1–3 (p.24), with Σ_M ≅ P(L).
   - A lieu x is 'ponctuel' (a 'point of M') if, for every figure X, x|∘|X ⇔ x ∉ omb°(X).
   - In particular, between points, x|∘|y ⇔ x ≠ y.
   - Ponctuaire magasins are the local ones all of whose lieux are points.

5. Magasins ensemblistes: a set L together with M ⊂ Figél(L), a set of 'elementary figures' in L; axioms Magens 1–2 (p.9).
   - The side note says these are the only magasins matching the more or less commonly accepted notions of 'topology', i.e. point-set frameworks.

6. Magasins ensemblistes modérés: add axiom Magens 3.
   - They correspond to 'tame topologies', which he says have so far been developed only for the piecewise-linear structure on R.

7. Side branch, maquettes: (M, ≤) with ≤ an order relation (Mag 1, p.25) and Σ_M ≅ P(M).
   - These are posets, i.e. T0 Alexandrov spaces, used as combinatorial models.
   - NB 1: a maquette (equivalently a T0 Alexandrov space) is a local or ponctuaire magasin only if it is discrete.
   - NB 2: there are tame non-set-theoretic magasins, for example maquettes.

The bottom NB fixes notation:
- ⊴ for incidence inside M, and ◁ for strict incidence;
- a separate symbol for incidence between M and the figures F;
- ⊆, or ⊆ with F above it, for inclusion of figures;
- possibly ≤ with s above it for subdivisions.

This prepares the next page, which introduces oriented 'magons': incidence posets with an orientation-reversing involution and a diamond-type axiom in codimension 2, i.e. axioms for oriented cell complexes.

Purpose: an axiomatic, possibly pointless, foundation for tame topology. Figures and the relations incidence, interiority and apartness are primitive. Points, supports and the classical point-set picture appear only as special cases. Combinatorial models (posets/maquettes) and genuine tame spaces are placed in one hierarchy.
errors: Historical claim slightly inaccurate: 'topologies modérées ... développées à présent que pour la seule structure linéaire par morceaux sur R'. By 1986 semialgebraic geometry and subanalytic geometry (Łojasiewicz, Hironaka) were well developed. O-minimality (Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn 1984–86) was just appearing. Grothendieck presumably means within his own axiomatic framework, but as stated it understates the existing literature.

Nothing checkable is proved on this page. The only factual claim is that a T0 maquette is local or ponctuaire only if discrete. This is plausible: if x < y in the specialization order, x lies in the closure of y and cannot be 'apart' from y, contradicting x|∘|y ⇔ x≠y. It depends on the unseen axioms Magloc/Magponc.

The diagram's arrows are not fully consistent with the text. Ponctuaire is described as 'local with all lieux ponctuels', yet it is also placed below the 'fidèles' branch. This suggests ponctuaire = local ∩ fidèle, which is stated only implicitly.

ideas.what: Axiomatic topology based on figures (regions) as primitives, with incidence ≤, a 'well-inside/interior' relation ≪, and an apartness relation |∘|; points recovered only in special cases (ponctuaire magasins)
ideas.modern_name: Point-free topology / mereotopology; contact and proximity algebras (well-inside relation as in de Vries algebras); Region Connection Calculus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Čech/Efremovič proximity spaces (1950s), de Vries (1962), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992), Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s); locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 calls for an axiomatic tame topology but gives no such axiomatics; to my knowledge the 'magasin' axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Support/shadow map X ↦ Omb°(X) into subsets of 'lieux', with disjoint supports ⇔ apartness; faithfulness condition (magasins à ombres fidèles)
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a contact/region algebra by regions of a space (Stone/de Vries-type duality); support maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Vries (1962); Düntsch–Winter, Dimov–Vakarelov representation theorems for contact algebras (2000s)

ideas.what: Definition of a 'point' of an abstract magasin as a lieu x with x|∘|X ⇔ x ∉ omb°(X)
ideas.modern_name: Points as maximal/prime filters or 'clans' in contact algebras; points of a locale

ideas.what: Maquettes: posets (= T0 Alexandrov spaces) treated as tame but non-set-theoretic magasins, i.e. combinatorial models inside the same axiomatic hierarchy as tame spaces
ideas.modern_name: Finite topological spaces / face posets as models of polyhedra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord and Stong (1966); later Barmak–Minian

ideas.what: Tame ('modérée') set-theoretic magasins: a set L with a class of elementary figures Figél(L) satisfying an extra tameness axiom Magens 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86); van den Dries' book 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures' (1998)
ideas.where_published: The programme (not these axioms) appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 and Récoltes et Semailles

ideas.what: Notation conventions: incidence ⊴ / strict incidence ◁, inclusion of figures, subdivisions

missed.claim: Around 1986, in the 'magasins' axiomatics, Grothendieck independently arrived at what is essentially a mereotopology or contact-algebra framework for tame topology. Regions are primitive, with an interior/well-inside relation and a disjointness (apartness) relation. Points are recovered via 'ponctuel' lieux, and set-theoretic topology is a special case. The mereotopology/contact-algebra literature does not cite him, and the tame-topology literature (o-minimality) never went pointless in this way.
missed.quote: Un lieu x ∈ L est dit "ponctuel" ou "un point" de M si ∀X ∈ M, x|∘|X ⇔ x ∉ omb°(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a point-free formulation of o-minimal/tame geometry in which definable regions and their contact relations are primitive. That links o-minimality with contact algebras / qualitative spatial reasoning, and with the representation theorems of Dimov–Vakarelov and Düntsch–Winter, which is a largely unexplored bridge.

missed.claim: A hierarchy of axiomatic structures (général → local / fidèle → ponctuaire → ensembliste → ensembliste modéré, plus maquettes) whose axioms sit on pp.9, 22–25, 31 of the manuscript. As far as I know, this classification was never published or developed by others.
missed.quote: Magasins ensemblistes modérés ... Correspondant aux "topologies modérées", qui n'ont été développées à présent que pour la seule structure linéaire par morceaux sur R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's own concrete attempt at the axiomatic tame topology announced in the Esquisse remains unexamined; comparing it with o-minimality and with point-free topology could be historically and mathematically informative.

missed.claim: Combinatorial models (posets/maquettes, and the oriented 'magons' of the next page) and tame spaces are treated as instances of a single notion, with an explicit criterion separating them: a T0 maquette is local only if discrete.
missed.quote: NB Il y a des magasins modérés non ensemblistes p. ex. les maquettes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates unifying finite-space / face-poset models and genuine tame spaces in one category, which relates to later work on finite spaces (Barmak–Minian) and on exit-path/stratified combinatorics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an overview diagram, not a result. Still, it documents an unpublished, essentially point-free (mereotopological) axiomatics for tame topology, with apartness and well-inside relations and recovered points. This seems not to be known to either the o-minimal or the mereotopology communities. It is interesting historically, but the content is definitional and programmatic.
transcription_corrections: The note beside the arrow from ponctuaires to ensemblistes reads roughly 'Ce sont les seuls magasins qui correspondent aux [notions] plus ou moins communément admises pour "la topologie"'. It annotates the magasins ensemblistes.
In the NB on ponctuel lieux the corrected wording is 'Les magasins "ponctuaires" sont les magasins locaux dont tous les lieux sont ponctuels' ('ponctuels' was replaced by 'ponctuaires' in the title).
Maquette NB: likely 'Une maquette, ou espace top. satisfaisant l'axiome de séparation T0, n'est un magasin local (ou ponctuel) que si elle est discrète'; 'pas' seems a misreading.
Last line of the tame-topology note: 'pour la seule structure linéaire par morceaux sur R'.
The interior relation in the local and fidèle magasins is written ≪ with a small circle (≪̊); the general and ponctuaire magasins appear to carry plain ≪.
